title: Design System: Landlord Ledger — Bank Passbook

ink-soft.derivation: ink at 72% alpha — secondary text, labels, quiet rows

ink-faint.derivation: ink at 66% alpha — placeholders, the resting delete icons, the register's type icons, the trend's sublabel, the least-important affordances

print-wash.derivation: print at 6% alpha — the balance rail's and the register's Net cell ground, rail hover, skeleton tint

print-soft.derivation: premixed print tint — the selected rail entry's ground; also the shadcn secondary/muted/accent slot (130 22% 93%)

rule.derivation: print at 38% alpha — the 1px hairline on rows, fields, dividers

page-title.purpose: Each route's own heading — the page's one h1; the product name in the header is a styled link home, not a heading. Body-scale bold ink; the world has no display face. The Properties register's line names print as h2s beneath the page's h1.

caption.purpose: The world's micro-label: field labels, table headers, strip labels, the tfoot legend, the caveat above the ledger (which names why the view differs — filtered, sorted, or both), the Reset control. Uppercase; tracking stops at 0.14em (fields), 0.16em (table headers), 0.18em (totals legends and stamp marks).

body.purpose: Form input text, tab labels, quiet controls; weight 600 on controls that act — the active tab owns 600, the inactive 500, each state alone.

ledger.purpose: Every ledger cell — dates, descriptions, categories, amounts, balances — and the Properties register's figures (Net, Income, Expenses at the 13px step; Units and the type label at 12.5px). IBM Plex Mono with tabular numerals.

totals-figure.purpose: The totals strip's Income / Expenses / Net — the largest figures on any page, still mono and tabular; Income prints green on every surface that carries it.

stamp-mark.purpose: Validation alert, the rotated delete-confirm question, and the export's acknowledgment stamp; the same 11px mono carries the sort arrows, the trend sublabel (mixed-case at 0.05em tracking), and the register's status marks — the ramp's caption floor.

shadows.name: floating-md
shadows.purpose: The single soft shadow a floating surface is allowed — the Radix Select option list (Tailwind shadow-md).

shadows.name: floating-lg
shadows.purpose: The dialog panel (over its 35% ink wash), the destructive confirm (inline cluster at sm and up, fixed bottom sheet below), the export stamp, and the delete-undo snackbar — every floating surface casts this one soft shadow. The page at rest casts nothing.

motion.name: ease-print
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out — the only authored easing.

motion.name: ledger-line-printed
motion.value: line-printed 500ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) both, fade-in 500ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) both
motion.purpose: The one authored motion: a row appearing after first paint wipes in left-to-right (clip-path inset(0 100% 0 0) to inset(0 0 0 0)) with a simultaneous fade — the balance figure lands last. First paint is still; a restored line (the undo's own small ceremony) prints back in too. Removed entirely under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Hover and focus are color/opacity states, not motion. The skeleton pulse is a stock utility; the one remaining spin (the deferred Add-Property modal) is stock too, not authored.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: The world's one behavior breakpoint: the rail expands or collapses (captions below, tooltips and toggle above), the header composes into one line and the masthead's primary returns from its 44px touch height to the 2.25rem control line, gutters widen to 2.25rem. useIsDesktop mirrors it via matchMedia, SSR-safe.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: The mobile-discipline breakpoint, live as state (useMediaQuery, SSR-safe): the filters fold behind their 'Filters · N' disclosure, the ledger sheet holds its 64rem print width with a frozen date column (at sm and up the sheet floors at 55rem instead), the destructive confirm pins as a bottom sheet with 44px targets — gated by the live query, so the sheet is absent from the desktop DOM — and the Undo target grows to 44px.

passbookRules.name: hairline
passbookRules.detail: border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(46, 94, 78, 0.38) — every ledger and register row, field edge, and internal divider.

passbookRules.name: totals
passbookRules.detail: The accountant's closing line, owned by exactly one side of its seam: .rule-totals on a top edge (the empty page's 'No entries' line), .rule-totals-b on the bottom edge of the row that closes the sheet — the last entry when no blank lines follow, the last blank line when they do. Spelled once each, deterministic against Tailwind's all-sides border-color utilities.

passbookRules.name: strip-edges
passbookRules.detail: The totals strip anchors itself with per-side utilities — border-t-print above, border-b-rule below — so no all-sides border-color can quietly win the anchor.

passbookRules.name: row-density
passbookRules.detail: --passbook-row, declared; realized as 0.625rem cell padding plus the 0.8125rem ledger line and the 1px row rule — one line at print density, held at real widths (1280 and 1440 both); the destructive control lives in the reserved trailing cell, not in the prose.

passbookRules.name: sheet-floor
passbookRules.value: 55rem at sm and up; 64rem below sm
passbookRules.detail: The table-fixed print width: the fixed column budget (Date 7.5rem / Description the fixed-layout remainder / Category 7.5rem / Property 7.5rem / Amount 7.5rem / Balance 8rem / Actions 2.75rem) that holds one-line rows, with long text truncating under pressure and the full text in the title; below sm the wider sheet slides inside its ruled region with the date column frozen at the left edge.

passbookRules.name: control-density
passbookRules.detail: --passbook-control: every field, select trigger, and primary button is h-9 at lg and up; wherever a thumb owns the surface the touch standard is 44px instead (masthead primary below lg, bottom-sheet confirms, Undo).

passbookRules.name: blank-line
passbookRules.detail: The unfilled printed lines below the last entry, ruled at the entries' own rhythm — aria-hidden, pointer-events none, capped at fifteen.

passbookRules.name: mount-gate
passbookRules.detail: The server snapshot is '[]' by design: the blank ruled lines compute after mount (server and client paint identically), and the empty page's 'No entries' is gated the same way — the region stays quiet through the hydration window so the first honest paint is silent and the ruled line belongs to the live snapshot alone.

passbookRules.name: radius
passbookRules.detail: The world's only corner (rounded-[2px]); the shadcn --radius base is re-pointed to 0.125rem so its lg/md steps collapse to the same 2px.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one ink primary per screen — the masthead's: ink ground, paper text, squared; "+ Add transaction" in the header, 44px high and full-width below lg (the masthead's touch standard), back to the 2.25rem control line at lg. The rail's "Add Property" has stepped down to a quiet outline, so the masthead keeps the screen's one ink primary.

records.title: The stamp-red renegotiation
records.body: The original direction contract carried an over-budget mark in stamp red; it had no trigger — no budget concept exists in the product. No budget scope was added. Stamp-red's standing role is state marks only (destructive confirms, validation failures), never decoration. The over-budget row tint retired with the first-viewport plan; the built ledger's rows carry no such mark.

records.title: The deferred unknown-category edge
records.body: A transaction already in storage whose category string is not one of the app's category records is unreachable through the app's own form (the form's Category select offers only INCOME_CATEGORIES / EXPENSE_CATEGORIES) and can never be isolated by the ledger's category filter, which lists the same records. In the built code the row itself still renders, printing its raw stored category string in the Category cell and totaling into every summary; what is truly unreachable is its creation and its isolation, not its display. The edge is deferred rather than resolved — no semantics (validation, migration, display treatment) were decided, and this record exists so a future change decides them deliberately instead of inheriting an accident.

records.title: The two known contextual detector flags
records.body: Two real deviations survive every pass, both in the browser's chrome rather than the world's surfaces, and both are deliberately left alone: the scrollbar thumb's 5px radius (styles.css — the one corner outside the 2px system) and the devtools widget's own panel headings (the TanStack devtools mounted in the root route render h3s that trip the heading-order detector — dev chrome outside the world's landmarks, dev-only and stripped from production builds by the devtools vite plugin's remove-devtools-on-build pass, so no shipped page carries them). Neither is a pattern to extend; this record exists so a future audit recognizes them instead of re-litigating them.

records.title: The round-three queued ledger
records.body: The third pass's picked fronts are closed in the build; four remain queued in the change's task ledger (§8), recorded as queued work, not canonized: the reading-column rebalance (description truncation at 1280), Unknown-Property denormalization + a property-delete line warning, the undo snackbar re-pin + a permanent-deletion status + the entry-editing path, and the filtered-empty "No matches" wiring. Code-verified context for two of them: the ledger's Property cell prints an "Unknown Property" fallback for a stored id with no property record, and a filter that empties the sheet still meets the scoped "No entries" line.

narrative.overview:
The ledger reads the way a bank records money. The surface is a passbook page: ivory paper carries dense printed columns ruled in machine-print green hairlines, every date and peso figure is set in IBM Plex Mono with tabular numerals at print density, and a running balance marches down the right edge on a pale print wash so the eye can audit the month by running down the rail. The category's default — a dashboard of white cards floating on a gray ground — is refused wholesale: no cards, no shadows at rest, no chart rings. Every total is a ruled printed strip, the trend is a ruled table, and the empty ledger is a ruled line, never an illustrated panel.

Depth comes from rules and ground, never elevation. Ink navy does the reading; print green is the machine's voice — it owns the hairline grid, income figures, focus, selection, and the selected rail's wash; stamp red is held out for state marks only, the red of a rubber stamp landing on a confirmation or a rejected line. The browser surfaces carry the world too: selection, caret, native accents, link underlines, and scrollbars are all passbook-toned, the cheap tell that it was built rather than assembled. One authored motion exists — a newly recorded line prints itself onto the page — and nothing else animates; hover and focus are color states, not motion.

The world is an Operate surface: a landlord completing bookkeeping, where scanability, density, and trust outrank expression. The finished world covers the shell (rail, header, tabs, footer), the Overview, Transactions, and Properties views, and the shared primitives; the Properties page has had its register pass — the card grid retired wholesale, one ruled line per property answering the product question in money (Net on the print wash first, Income in green, Expenses in ink-soft), the ledger's own trailing-cell delete and stamp confirm — and the third pass tightened the record's own truths: every user-visible date now derives from local parts (The Local-Date Rule), the export writes the displayed slice and says so on its control, its stamp, and its filename, and the empty page's paint is mount-gated so the first honest paint is silent. The record tells the truth about itself: the shell's footer names where the data lives on every page, the export's stamp names the slice that was written, and a delete carries a five-second undo. Two deferrals remain, both recorded, not canonized: the Add-Property modal's native checkbox and pending spinner, and the unlinked Reports placeholder; round three's unpicked fronts are queued in the change's records, not canonized here.
keyCharacteristics: Ivory paper ground (#fbf8f1), ink-navy type (#1b2a41), machine-print green hairline rules (#2e5e4e), stamp red (#a31621) reserved for state marks.
IBM Plex Mono with tabular numerals for every date and money figure, at print density (0.8125rem line; one-line rows ≈39.84px, held at real widths).

Every user-visible date tells the local truth: a stored date is a calendar name, never a UTC instant, and the one format module owns every derivation (The Local-Date Rule, verified under TZ=Asia/Manila and TZ=America/New_York).
Structure from rules — 1px hairlines everywhere, a 3px double totals rule for closing lines — never from shadows.

The running balance rail on a print wash down the ledger's right edge always accumulates the book (every entry, date ascending) whatever the display; the caveat "Balance follows the book" prints whenever the view is not the book's own order and names why — "this view is filtered", "sorted newest first", or both.
Properties is a ruled register, not a card grid: one line per property, Net on the print wash first, Income in green, Expenses in ink-soft, the delete in the reserved trailing margin.
One authored motion (the print-in), removed entirely under prefers-reduced-motion; a restored line prints back in too.

Honesty signals throughout: the footer's storage note, the export's stamp acknowledgment naming the slice it wrote (all entries at rest, the displayed ledger whenever anything narrows), the five-second delete undo that restores the original id.
2px corners everywhere: squared, printed form fields.

rules.name: The Stamp Rule
rules.body: Stamp red is a state mark only: destructive confirms and validation failures, always uppercase mono, always bordered or grounded — never a tint, tint never a decoration. If the red doesn't say "act on me" or "this was rejected," it doesn't appear.

rules.name: The Owned Browser Chrome Rule
rules.body: Selection prints as print green at 22% over paper with ink text; carets and native checkbox/radio accents are print green; links carry ink text over a 1px print underline at 3px offset, turning print green on hover; scrollbars are thin ink (34% alpha) on a transparent track with a paper-framed thumb. The world does not stop at the components.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Rule
rules.body: Every figure — money, dates, counts — is set in IBM Plex Mono with tabular numerals, so columns of pesos align down the page like a printed ledger. Money is formatted by the one formatMoney (₱, exactly two fraction digits everywhere) and dates by the one formatDate (en-US); no surface re-creates a local copy, and the sans face never sets a figure — the form's date and amount inputs print in the mono face with tabular numerals, a date inside a field no less than a date on the page.

rules.name: The Local-Date Rule
rules.body: Every user-visible date derives from local parts, and localDateString/localMonthKey in src/lib/format.ts are the one source of date truth. A stored date is a calendar string ('YYYY-MM-DD') — the name of a day on the page, not a UTC instant — so formatDate parses the string's own parts and never hands it to the bare ISO constructor (which reads UTC midnight and prints the day before everywhere west of UTC). The form's blank line and the export's filename stamp write localDateString; the current-month check and the trend buckets compare a stored string's own prefix against localMonthKey, each bucket month derived from local parts with the day pinned to the 1st, so a 31st can never skip a bucket; the carried-forward label reads the stored string's parts the same way. No surface reaches for toISOString, whose UTC day is yesterday's page for most of a UTC+8 morning. Verified under TZ=Asia/Manila and TZ=America/New_York.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: The page never casts shadows; a floating surface may cast one, softly. Hover on a page element changes color, never elevation.

rules.name: The Book-Authority Rule
rules.body: The running balance is the book's, not the view's: it always accumulates every entry in date-ascending order, whatever slice or sort the page displays, and the caveat names the divergence — and why ("this view is filtered", "sorted newest first", or both) — whenever the display is not the book itself. A rail that recomputed per view would print accounts that never existed.

rules.name: The One Authored Motion
rules.body: A row that appears after first paint prints itself onto the page: a left-to-right clip-path wipe plus a fade, 500ms, exponential ease-out, the balance figure landing last. First paint is still; a restored line (the undo's own small ceremony) prints back in too. prefers-reduced-motion removes it entirely. Nothing else is authored: hovers transition color/opacity only, the skeleton keeps its stock pulse, and the one remaining spin (the deferred Add-Property modal) is stock, not authored.

dos: Do set every figure in IBM Plex Mono with tabular numerals, formatted through the one formatMoney (₱, two fraction digits always) and the one formatDate.

Do tell the local truth in every date: a stored string is a calendar name, not a UTC instant — parse its parts (formatDate), write local parts (localDateString), bucket by parts with the day pinned to the 1st (localMonthKey), and never reach for toISOString or the bare ISO constructor on a stored string (The Local-Date Rule).
Do build structure from the rules: 1px hairlines for rows, fields, and dividers; the 3px double totals rule for closing lines; print underlines for headers and the active tab.

Do keep the rail on the book: it always accumulates every entry, date ascending, whatever the page displays (sorting removal is off, so the sheet opens chronological), and the caveat "Balance follows the book" prints whenever the display differs — any active filter, any sort that is not date-ascending — naming why: "this view is filtered", "sorted newest first", or both. No caveat in the book's own order.
Do name every totals claim honestly: the strip's label and aria-label total exactly the slice its page displays, and say which page semantics they carry ("Displayed ledger" vs "All entries").

Do write the displayed slice and say so: the export control reads "Export CSV · All entries" at rest and "Export CSV · Displayed ledger" whenever anything narrows, the stamp and the CSV's filename name the same slice, at rest the displayed slice IS the book (the footer's backup promise holds exactly), and the Transactions header's count caption names what filters hide — "N of M entries" against the property scope's total, the plain count at rest; Overview keeps totaling the pure scope, never the ledger's filters.
Do say where the record lives and what each write did: the footer's storage note on every page, the export's stamp acknowledgment, and the delete's five-second undo restoring the original id.
Do keep every actionable surface on the 2px print outline (or the field ring) on focus-visible — rail, toggle, tabs, disclosure, delete control — never the browser default.
Do keep stamp red for state marks only — destructive confirms and validation failures — squared, uppercase mono, bordered or grounded.
Do keep one ink primary per screen — the masthead's "+ Add transaction"; the rail's "Add Property" is a quiet outline, and everything else is quiet ink.
Do keep every overflow inside its own ruled region (tables and the tab row scroll; the main column floors at min-w-0) so the paper never leaks at 390px.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion by removing the print-in entirely.
Do keep the form's validation to one voice: the authored stamp names only the actually-missing fields, read as a person says them — no native `required` bubbles.

Do keep every accelerator honest: "Reset filters" prints only when there is something to reset and unwinds exactly the counted controls; "/" reaches the search field unless the hand is already writing in a field; the dialog's every close path returns focus to the trigger that opened it.

Do carry the 44px touch standard wherever a thumb owns the surface — the masthead's primary below lg, the form's radios by label padding, the ledger's sort headers grown by padding (the caption type never grows to fake it), the bottom-sheet confirms, the Undo — while the desktop control line stays 2.25rem.
Do keep the skip link the document's first Tab stop — quiet until it holds focus, then the printed ink stamp at the page's corner, landing on #main-content.
donts: Don't put shadows on the page at rest — only a floating surface gets one, softly.
Don't invent a budget mark, an over-budget row tint, or any other stamp-red decoration; no budget concept exists in the product (renegotiated 2026-11-21).
Don't set money in the sans face, drop the fraction digits, or re-create a local formatter.
Don't reach for toISOString or hand a stored date to the bare ISO constructor — the stored string is a calendar name, not a UTC instant (The Local-Date Rule).
Don't round past 2px, and don't introduce pills, rings, or cards — the Properties register retired the world's one card grid; no built surface ships a card.

Don't sew a destructive word into the record: the delete control is an icon in the sheet's reserved trailing margin, revealed on hover, focus, or touch — never a caption link inside the description line.
Don't replace the ruled empty state with a card or illustration.
Don't animate anything beyond the print-in; hover and focus are color states.
Don't spend print green on decoration — it belongs to rules, income, focus, selection, and the rail's selected state.

Don't inherit the two recorded deferrals — the Add-Property modal's native gray-bordered checkbox and pending spinner, and the unlinked /reports placeholder's raw template chrome; they are recorded, not canonized.
